summary: An April 1st joke RFC that purports to establish a Protocol Police, a body to assess and enforce correct protocol behavior. It plays on the IETF saying We are not the Protocol Police. It is humorous and not a real standard or organization.

plainLanguage.summary: A joke document that pretends the Internet's rule-makers have created a police force to hand out tickets to badly behaved computer programs.

subtitle: An April Fools establishment of a secret police force to enforce protocol compliance.

tldr.problem: The IETF repeatedly says, "We are not the Protocol Police," whenever someone complains about non-compliant implementations. This creates confusion about who enforces standards.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8962 formally establishes the Protocol Police, a secret body selected by NomCom to enforce IETF protocols with punishments including traffic imprisonment and TCP resets.
tldr.outcome: This April 1st joke exposes the tension between the IETF's collaborative philosophy and the reality that non-compliance goes unpunished. It is pure satire.

today: RFC 8962 is an April Fools RFC from 2021, published for informational purposes. The Protocol Police do not exist and this is purely satirical.

sections.title: Establishing the Police
sections.content:
The IETF has a saying: "We are not the Protocol Police." This is used whenever someone wants to punish non-compliant implementations. RFC 8962 takes this seriously and formally establishes the Protocol Police, a secret body appointed by the IETF's NomCom (Nominating Committee) to enforce IETF standards.

The RFC is written in authoritative, official language: the Protocol Police will assess and enforce correct protocol behavior. Members are not publicly named, enabling them to operate without interference. The first rule of the Protocol Police is $CIPHERTEXT (a reference to Fight Club's "first rule").
sections.plainLanguage: It jokes that the IETF actually created a secret enforcement agency to punish anyone who breaks protocol rules.

sections.title: Offenses and Punishments
sections.content:
The Protocol Police enforce three categories of offense: protocol-layer violations (crossing layer boundaries), deliberate non-interoperability (creating walled gardens), and disobeying RFCs.

Punishment takes the form of traffic imprisonment: the Protocol Police maintain a list of offending hosts and other networks drop all packets from them. Using machine-learning threat analysis, they identify likely non-compliant networks and discipline them with TCP reset packets. The RFC jokes that "the Protocol Police always shoot from the HIP" (Heuristic Internet Policing).
sections.plainLanguage: Bad implementations get quarantined and have their traffic cut off by everyone else on the internet, delivered with TCP reset packets.

sections.title: Jurisdiction and Oversight
sections.content:
Offenses should be reported to /dev/null (a Unix trash file), where the Protocol Police are always listening. The RFC includes sections on Security Considerations ("Before the Protocol Police, there was no security"), Privacy Considerations ("None"), and Human Rights Considerations ("There are none for you to worry about").

On oversight: all police forces must be accountable, and the Protocol Police "take full responsibility for oversight of their actions and promise to overlook all activities," a tautology that satirizes bureaucratic accountability.
sections.plainLanguage: It jokes that the police report to a garbage file, protect no one's rights, and are accountable only to themselves.

sections.title: The Satire
sections.content:
RFC 8962 satirizes the gap between the IETF's open consensus-driven philosophy and the lack of enforcement when implementers ignore standards. It mocks the phrase "We are not the Protocol Police" by taking it literally, then filling the RFC with bureaucratic language, absurd definitions, and dark humor.

Published April 1, 2021, as informational, the RFC is purely satirical and the Protocol Police do not exist.
sections.plainLanguage: It shows how the internet's collaborative system has no real way to punish rule-breakers, then jokes about creating a secret police force to fix the problem.
